clue.text: Sets out to make this town his own — taking what?

definitions.meaning: to set out on a journey is to depart or start off towards somewhere

definitions.text: to make this town his own — taking what?
definitions.meaning: the first letters must come off the two words this and town to leave his and own, so the question asks what is removed

explanation.surface: A conqueror sets out to claim a town for himself, and we ask what he will seize.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a riddle: remove the first letter of THIS and of TOWN and you get HIS and OWN, so what you take off are their heads.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who heads off is departing on a route, a plain synonym for setting out.

clue.text: Scaly reptile one year not found in the country

parts.note: the Roman numeral one is I

indicators.note: the letter for year is missing from the country named, so it is taken away

parts.note: Guyana is a country in South America

explanation.surface: A reptile is said to be unknown in a certain country for a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not found in' removes the year's letter from the South American country; 'one' is the Roman numeral that leads.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large lizard of the Americas with scaly skin, an example of the class.

clue.text: Consummate love via embraces

indicators.note: one word holding another in its arms means it goes around it

parts.note: going via a place means passing through it
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Love is consummated by way of an embrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love via embraces' reads as via embracing love: THROUGH wraps O, giving THR-O-OUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Consummate as an adjective means complete or utter, the same sense as a thorough job.

clue.text: Clash over place for member of warrior caste

indicators.note: in an across clue over can mean the preceding word is turned round

parts.note: to jar is to clash or grate
to put something is to place it

explanation.surface: A conflict breaks out over where a member of a warrior class may stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns JAR into RAJ.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rajputs are a north Indian people traditionally of the Kshatriya or warrior caste.

clue.text: Shortly after Conservative becomes a clergyman

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other, so the second sits behind the first

parts.note: anon is an old word meaning soon or shortly

explanation.surface: Soon after joining the Tories, a man takes holy orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' looks like it means abbreviated, but it is the word ANON.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a member of the clergy attached to a cathedral chapter, a specific kind of churchman.

clue.text: Kitchen tool that's definitely not new shown in one drawing?

indicators.note: these pieces are displayed inside the other word, so they go into it

parts.note: one who draws, as in a tied game, could be called a tier
nope is an emphatic informal no

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget, plainly not new, appears in someone's sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' suggests art, but it is drawing a match: a tier is one who ties. NOPEN goes inside TIER as TI-NOPEN-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin opener is a device for opening cans, found in most kitchens.

clue.text: Shine as a specialist may do using two languages

definitions.text: Shine as a specialist may do

parts.note: French is the language of France
Polish is the language of Poland

explanation.surface: A craftsman buffs a surface while speaking two tongues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' changes sound and sense: the language, and the verb to shine.
explanation.definitionFit: French polishing is a skilled cabinetmaker's technique giving wood a glossy shellac finish.

clue.text: Person allowing no opposition to Italian art forms

indicators.note: the letters are formed into new shapes, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dictator imposes forms on Italian art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forms' looks like a noun for art styles but is the signal to rearrange the two words after it; 'to' stays as written at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A totalitarian supports a regime that tolerates no rival parties or dissent.

clue.text: Heavenly body — one a Parisienne possesses in Frenchman's city

parts.note: Mars is a planet

indicators.note: to possess is to hold within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: elle is French for she, a Parisian woman
the Roman numeral one is I

explanation.surface: A planet and a Parisian woman share a city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word for she is a crossword staple for a Frenchwoman; 'possesses' puts the numeral inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Marseille is the French spelling of the great Mediterranean port, so a Frenchman's name for it.

clue.text: Good and bad rounds start off regular quiz

indicators.note: to round something is to go around it, so these letters enclose the next

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects

indicators.note: the start of the word means just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A regular quiz begins with good and bad rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounds' suggests quiz rounds but signals G-ILL going around R.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill someone is to question them intensively, a verb sense of interrogate.

clue.text: Sort of letter (permit) a licensee holds

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer within its run of letters

explanation.surface: A licence is held by someone selling drinks, in a particular typeface.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is in permIT A LICensee.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic letters are a sloping typeface, a style or sort of printed character.

clue.text: Component containing blue weedkiller

indicators.note: one word holding another around it, so the second goes inside

parts.note: a part is a component
aqua is a light greenish-blue colour

explanation.surface: An ingredient with a blue tint is used in weed killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' has the component wrap the colour between its third and fourth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraquat is a highly toxic herbicide used to destroy weeds.

clue.text: Bug going round hospital in isolated area

indicators.note: the phrase encircles the next letter, which goes within it

parts.note: to bug someone is to get to them, annoy them
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: An insect circles a hospital in a cut-off zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' is the insect on the surface, but means annoy: GET TO, holding H.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghetto is a segregated district where a group lives apart from the rest.

clue.text: Train seat a man is in, someone vacated?

indicators.note: the man sits inside the seat, so his letters go inside

parts.note: rear is a euphemism for one's seat or bottom
he refers to a man

indicators.note: emptied of its middle, leaving only the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: On a train, a man occupies a seat someone has just left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a railway, but it is the verb practise. REAR holds HE, then SE from someone emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise or drill, as actors train before a performance.

clue.text: Very modern couple stopped by police at last

indicators.note: the word is plugged by another, so that letter goes inside

parts.note: to hitch is to couple, as a trailer to a car

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A pair are finally pulled over by the police in something very modern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple' looks like a pair, but it is the verb HITCH, plugged by E.
explanation.definitionFit: Hi-tech describes advanced technology or contemporary styling.

clue.text: Answer sure to be everywhere?

parts.note: bound to happen means certain or sure to happen

explanation.surface: An answer that is certain to be everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sure to' together reads as bound to, with 'to' joining.
explanation.definitionFit: To abound is to exist in great numbers, so to be found all over.

clue.text: Rogue report about constant ordeal regularly viewed

indicators.note: one word sits about another, around it, so the second goes inside

parts.note: a report is a loud noise or sound
C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

indicators.note: only every other letter of the word is seen

explanation.surface: A villain's account of a constant trial is examined at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUND holds C, then REL from the even letters of oRdEaL.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is a dishonest rascal, a synonym for rogue.

clue.text: Taking flight after getting in trouble for scrapping speech

indicators.note: the letters fall into disorder, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone flees after trouble because of quarrelsome words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking flight' looks like the action, but its letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighting talk is belligerent language, speech for a scrap or fight.

clue.text: Sound astonished to be limiting Republican's understanding

indicators.note: putting limits round another, so it goes inside

parts.note: to gasp is to make a noise of astonishment
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Someone gasps at the limits of a Republican's understanding.
explanation.walkthrough: GASP is opened to admit R.
explanation.definitionFit: A grasp of something is a firm comprehension of it.

clue.text: Phone software design — one shown by Times Supplement

parts.note: an app is software for a phone
an end is a purpose or design
the Roman numeral one is I
x is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A phone app design shown in a newspaper's supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times Supplement' suggests the newspaper's add-on, but Times means multiply, X.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendix is added material at the end of a book, a supplement to it.

clue.text: Actuary in a state about hard rule applied without limitation

indicators.note: one set of letters goes around the other, enclosing it
being in a state means agitated, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An actuary is upset about strict rule imposed without limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' suggests a nation but means agitated: the anagram of ACTUARY goes about H.
explanation.definitionFit: Autarchy is absolute sovereignty or despotic power, rule with no checks.

clue.text: Individual on heroin and speed — the outcome's obvious here

parts.note: one means a single individual
horse is slang for heroin
to race is to speed

explanation.surface: Someone on heroin and speed — we all know how this ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link; 'speed' is not the drug but the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-horse race is a contest with a foregone conclusion because one competitor dominates.

clue.text: Way, initially defective, in which to order a drink

indicators.note: the following words go inside the other word
missing its first letter, so the opening is removed

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner
to range things is to order or arrange them

explanation.surface: A broken path where one goes to order a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially defective' drops the first letter of the word for way, leaving ODE; 'in which' puts RANGE and A after its O. ROAD does not work for 'Way'.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangeade is a sweet fizzy orange-flavoured drink.

clue.text: Match official, suppressing anger, impressed by con? That's puzzling

indicators.note: pressed inside the other, so it goes within

parts.note: a sting is a con trick

indicators.note: keeping down, so the word for anger is cut out

parts.note: an umpire officiates at a match
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A referee, holding back rage, is swayed by a con — it's baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressing' cuts anger out of the referee's title to leave UMP; 'impressed by' sets that inside the con.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumping means baffling or perplexing, an adjective for something puzzling.

clue.text: Succeeded with a great novel involving unknown character's daydream

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, in genealogy

indicators.note: taking in another letter, which goes inside
novel means new, so the letters take a new form

parts.note: Z is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A great novel with a mysterious character prompts a reverie.
explanation.walkthrough: A GREAT rearranged as TARGAE holds Z: TARGAZE.
explanation.definitionFit: To stargaze is to daydream, to have one's head in the clouds.

clue.text: Heard of person who beats the booze

indicators.note: the word is spoken, its sound giving the answer

parts.note: to lick is to beat, so a licker beats

explanation.surface: Rumours of someone overcoming drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beats the booze' suggests kicking alcohol; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquor is alcoholic spirits, a synonym for booze.

clue.text: Turn out a fool? What's up?

parts.note: a clot is a stupid person

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters go bottom to top

parts.note: eh is an interjection asking what

explanation.surface: Ejecting an idiot — what's going on?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn out' means dress, not eject. EH turned 'up' gives HE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be well turned out is to be well dressed, so turn out means clothe.

clue.text: Be prejudiced about women appearing topless

indicators.note: without its top, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: sexist means discriminating against women

explanation.surface: Being sexist about women going topless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be prejudiced' looks like one phrase; 'Be' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is simply to be, the verb of being.
